_comment: The data-collection plan. 89 requests across stages 0-4. owner_kind: HUMAN (only the company can know or decide), DOCUMENT (paste or upload existing material), AGENT_RESEARCH (a prompt for an outside AI assistant plus an import format, OR a plain form filled in by hand; a different person checks the assistant's output), DERIVED (the tool prepares it by itself). done_when is a JSON query (same DSL as the checks plus criterion_pass / gate_decided / derived_ran / all_done / any). why.criteria are check ids this request feeds; why_plain says in one specific sentence why we ask. Form fields: kind text|longtext|enum|number|date|bool|ref|lines; "lines" fields carry typed columns (text, number, date, choice, yesno, pick) so nobody types a code word or a record id. depth_level: the lowest depth at which the request is needed. minutes: estimated minutes of a person's time (0 for steps the tool does itself). Examples live in data/request_examples.json and depend on the product type and whether it is sold or internal.

S0-A.title: Sponsor kickoff
S0-A.purpose: Agree what the product is, who sponsors it, who else matters, and what material already exists.
S0-A.bring: Any memo or brief you already have, and notes from any customer conversation.
S0-A.outcome: A named sponsor, the people who matter, the problem written down and the sources behind the idea.

S0-B.title: Limits, assumptions and risks
S0-B.purpose: Write down the limits, the unproven assumptions and the worries before anything is promised.
S0-B.who: Product leader + CFO + Head of Ops
S0-B.bring: The budget figure, the date that cannot move, and your biggest worries.
S0-B.outcome: A list of limits, ranked assumptions and the main risks, each with an owner.

S0-C.title: Open questions, scope boundary and the Stage 0 sign-off
S0-C.purpose: Settle the open questions, draw the first scope line and decide whether to move on from Stage 0.
S0-C.bring: The list of things nobody can answer yet, and a rough idea of what is in and out.
S0-C.outcome: Questions settled or parked, a first scope line, an approved intake document and a decision.

S1-A.title: Customer and market truths
S1-A.purpose: Pin down who the customers are, what they are trying to get done and who they compare you with.
S1-A.bring: What you know about customers and their jobs, and the competitors or alternatives they compare you with.
S1-A.outcome: Customer groups, ranked jobs and a sized-up list of competitors or alternatives.

S1-B.title: Positioning, risks and the Stage 1 sign-off
S1-B.purpose: Decide how to position and price against competitors, test the riskiest guesses, get the legal scan signed and decide whether to move on from Stage 1.
S1-B.bring: Your riskiest assumptions, and the Legal person for the law and standards list.
S1-B.outcome: A pricing position, a test plan for risky assumptions, a signed legal scan and a decision.

S2-A.title: Scope workshop
S2-A.purpose: Decide what to build, in which parts, with what priority and how success is measured.
S2-A.bring: Your goals, a rough feature list and the effort estimates from the tech lead.
S2-A.outcome: Goals, success measures, a feature list with priorities and effort, and what is left out.

S2-B.title: Capacity, baseline and the Stage 2 sign-off
S2-B.purpose: Check the plan fits the team and the date, record the scope baseline and decide whether to move on from Stage 2.
S2-B.bring: The number of people and months you really have.
S2-B.outcome: A plan that fits the team, a first release, the sponsor's scope decision and a decision to move on.

S3-A.title: Requirements walkthrough
S3-A.purpose: Turn the scope into precise requirements, rules and targets that can be tested.
S3-A.who: Product leader + BA + tech lead + Legal
S3-A.bring: The business rules and the speed and reliability numbers.
S3-A.outcome: Reviewed requirements, business rules, quality targets and a user for each story.

S3-B.title: Quality review and the Stage 3 sign-off
S3-B.purpose: Check the acceptance tests and open questions and decide whether to move on from Stage 3.
S3-B.bring: The drafted tests and any unanswered questions.
S3-B.outcome: Reviewed tests, no open must-answer questions, an approved requirements document and a decision.

S4-A.title: Flow walkthrough
S4-A.purpose: Walk the main flows from start to end, including what happens when a step fails.
S4-A.bring: The main processes and what goes wrong in them.
S4-A.outcome: Named flows with failure paths, a life cycle for the main record, and reviewed flow drafts.

S4-B.title: Handover and the Stage 4 sign-off
S4-B.purpose: Settle the last questions, confirm the flows and decide whether to move on and hand over to the developers.
S4-B.outcome: Approved stories ready to go to the developers.
